title: Survivors T_{n,l,b}, sign reconciliation, and the positive formula

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma G4.** Prove the main theorem (`\ref{thm:improved-coefficient-formula}`):
$$c_{(a,1^b)}(n)=\#\{w\in\OSP(n,n-b)\ :\ \inv(w)=a,\ w\text{ is type I}\}.$$

Take $\ell=a+2b$, so $S_{n,a+2b,b}=\bigcup_{i=0}^b\{w\in\OSP(n,n-b+i):\inv(w)=a+i\}$ matches $(\star)$ under $c=i$, $\sgn(w)=(-1)^{n-\blocks(w)}=(-1)^c=(-1)^i$.

Two things must be proved in full:

1. **Survivor set.** $\phi$ pairs elements of $S$ with opposite signs and equal $q$-contribution **except** the type-I elements with $c=b$ that $\phi$ maps out of $S$ (Lemma G3(i)). Show the set of unpaired elements is exactly
$$T_{n,a+2b,b}=\{w\in\OSP(n,n-b):\inv(w)=a,\ w\text{ type I}\}.$$
Care: one must confirm $\phi$ is a genuine **involution within the paired part** (G3(ii)/(iii) give $\phi(w)\in S$ and $\phi$ is its own inverse), so cancellation is complete on $S\setminus T$.

2. **Sign reconciliation (most likely real gap).** Survivors lie in $\OSP(n,n-b)$, i.e. $c=b$, so $\sgn=(-1)^b$. The alternating sum $(\star)$ has leading sign $(-1)^b$ on the $i=b$ term. The proof must explicitly show the signed sum
$$\sum_{w\in S}(-1)^{c(w)}=\#T$$
reduces to a **plain positive count** of $T$ — i.e. that all survivors contribute $+1$ after factoring out the global structure — and that this equals $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)$ as given by $(\star)$. The current proof's final paragraph asserts this in one line without the sign reconciliation; this is exactly an "unjustified key step" (F3).

**Status:** positive formula $=$ alternating formula verified numerically for $n\le6$; $n=4$ table fully reproduced. The gap is the rigorous cancellation + sign argument.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Verified — issue resolved.**

I reviewed the current `solution.tex` and ran independent numerical checks. All three pieces flagged in this issue are now present and rigorous:

**1. Survivor set (cancellation).** `lem:classify` strata-tracks $\phi$ on $S_{n,\ell,b}$:
- (i) type I, $c=b$ ($\inv=\ell-2b$) $\Rightarrow \phi(w)\notin S$;
- (ii) type I, $c<b \Rightarrow \phi(w)\in S$, lands in $\OSP(n,n-(c+1))$;
- (iii) type II $\Rightarrow c>0$, $\phi(w)\in S$, lands in $\OSP(n,n-(c-1))$;
- (iv) type III impossible (would force $\ell=b>\lfloor(\ell-1)/2\rfloor$).

`lem:survivors` assembles these: $T_{n,\ell,b}\subseteq S$; $\phi$ maps $T$ out of $S$; and crucially it checks $\phi(w)\in S\setminus T$ in BOTH cases (ii) [image type II, never in $T$] and (iii) [image type I in $\OSP(n,n-(c-1))$, in $T$ only if $c=b+1$, impossible]. Since $\phi$ is a global involution (`lem:phi-props`), it restricts to a fixed-point-free (no type III) sign-reversing involution on $S\setminus T$, so cancellation on $S\setminus T$ is complete.

**2. Sign reconciliation.** With $\varepsilon(w)=(-1)^{\blocks(w)-(n-b)}=(-1)^{b-c}$, cases (ii)/(iii) flip $\blocks$ by $\pm1$, hence flip $\varepsilon$ — that is precisely why cancellation is sign-reversing. Survivors lie in $\OSP(n,n-b)$ so $c=b$ and $\varepsilon=(-1)^0=+1$; therefore $\sum_{w\in S}\varepsilon(w)=\#T$ is a genuine positive count (eq. `signed-sum`).

**3. Main theorem.** Setting $\ell=a+2b$ (so $b\le\lfloor(\ell-1)/2\rfloor$ and $\ell-2b=a$) and reindexing the alternating formula by $c=b-i$, the sign $(-1)^i=(-1)^{b-c}=\varepsilon(w)$ matches exactly, giving $c_{(a,1^b)}(n)=\#T_{n,a+2b,b}=\#\{w\in\OSP(n,n-b):\inv(w)=a,\text{ type I}\}$.

**Residual dependency closed.** The critic's last residual was `lem:phi-props`'s $\Delta\inv=\pm1$; this is now fully proved in the file via the crossing form `lem:inv-cross` and the position-of-large-values lemma `lem:large-values`.

**Numerical confirmation (this session):**
- $\phi$ is an involution with $(\Delta\blocks,\Delta\inv)=(-1,-1)$ on type I, $(+1,+1)$ on type II, fixing type III — verified exhaustively for $n=5$.
- The alternating formula `(first-formula-coeffs)` equals the positive formula `(second-formula-coeffs)` for ALL $(n,a,b)$ with $n\le6$, $1\le a<2n$, $0\le b<n$.

No further edits to `solution.tex` were needed; the gap described in this issue is closed. Resolving.
